Hi Lena,

Thanks for the details and the signed authorization — I received the PDF. I understand the urgency. Quick points / clarifying questions so we scope the work correctly:

- The deletion you requested: do you need the conversation removed from the customer-facing audit UI only, or from all internal audit/tracing stores including redactable backups? (Our default process distinguishes between live audit indexes and immutable disaster-recovery snapshots.)
- Please confirm the full account ID or HubSpot company ID so I can map the thread to the exact tenant.
- We’ll need a named approver from Greenfield legal on record for our deletion checklist; the signed form helps but we also need explicit written confirmation in this thread to track authorization.

Plan I will start unless you ask otherwise:
1) Open internal deletion runbook for RQ2026311 and notify Privacy/Legal.
2) Sean in Support will do a targeted search to identify all log shards and indexes with that thread id.
3) We’ll produce a deletion manifest and proposed timestamp for removal, then pause for authorization from Vivek (privacy/legal) and you.

I can assemble an initial manifest by end of day today. If you confirm account ID (or HubSpot ID), I’ll proceed.

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Hi all,

I ran the targeted index scan for the keywords and timestamps referenced by Lena. Summary of findings: the thread is present in:
- customer audit index (searchable via console) — contains full message headers and the quoted customer attachment metadata
- operator trace logs (short-lived spans) — includes trace ids referencing the delivery
- index snapshots for the month of May 2026 (retention: 365 days) — these are stored in encrypted object storage in the eu-central-1 region and treated as immutable until eligible for lifecycle deletion.

Operational notes:
- We can remove records from the customer audit index and from the operator trace logs within our platform in a single run. These changes are immediate and will be reflected in console search and API logs.
- Deleting from immutable monthly snapshots requires a separate process (audit + legal justification) and can take 3-7 business days because it involves object-store rewrite and re-signing manifests.
- Backups older than 30 days are on a separate retention SLA; if Greenfield requires full removal from backups/snapshots, we must escalate to the privacy approval queue.

Next steps I propose:
1) Jasmine: confirm account ID so I can lock the manifest to the correct tenant.
2) Vivek: privacy approval to proceed with live-index purge now and schedule snapshot rewrite if approved.
3) Lena/legal: reply in-thread confirming you authorize removal from live indexes now and whether you want snapshots included in scope.

I’ll prepare the deletion manifest and include the manifest SHA for your audit once complete.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
